prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A quick charging system for electrically driven vehicles and method for forming an electrically conductive connection between a vehicle and a stationary charging station having a contact device, a charging contact device, and a positioning device. The charging contact device can be electrically contacted in a contact position together with the contact device. The contact device can be positioned in the vertical and horizontal direction relative to the charging contact device and moved to the contact position. The contact device has a contact element carrier with contact elements that can each be electrically contacted together with charge contact elements of the charge contact device, forming contact pairs, in the contact position. A guide device is provided, such that, when the contact device and the charge contact device are brought together, a physical contacting of the contact elements together with the charge contact device is inhibited before reaching the contact position.

The charging contact device can be electrically contacted with the contact device in a contact position. outputs.L2: A rapid-charging arrangement for electric vehicles, along with a method for establishing an electrically conductive link between a vehicle and a fixed charging station, includes a contact unit, a charging contact unit, and a positioning unit. The charging contact unit is capable of making electrical contact with the contact unit when both are in a defined contact position. The contact unit can be aligned vertically and horizontally with respect to the charging contact unit and then moved into the contact position. The contact unit includes a carrier for contact elements, with each contact element being electrically connectable to a corresponding charging contact element of the charging contact unit, thereby creating contact pairs in the contact position. A guide mechanism is also included so that, as the contact unit and the charging contact unit are moved toward one another, the contact elements are prevented from physically touching the charging contact unit before the contact position is reached.
outputs.L3:
The system is designed to enable quick charging of electrically driven vehicles by establishing an electrically conductive connection between the vehicle and a stationary charging station. This allows electrical energy to be transferred efficiently from the charging station to the vehicle, making the system particularly suitable for rapid charging operations.

The system comprises a contact device, a charging contact device, and a positioning device. The contact device is arranged so that it can be moved relative to the charging contact device. In particular, the positioning device allows the contact device to be positioned both vertically and horizontally with respect to the charging contact device. As a result, the contact device can be accurately aligned and then moved into a defined contact position.

The contact device includes a contact element carrier on which a plurality of contact elements is arranged. When the contact device reaches the contact position, these contact elements come into electrical contact with corresponding charge contact elements of the charging contact device. In this state, an electrically conductive connection is formed between the vehicle and the stationary charging station, allowing charging current to flow.

The system also includes a guide device that controls the approach of the contact device toward the charging contact device. The guide device is configured to prevent the contact elements from physically touching the charging contact device before the contact position has been reached. This helps protect the contact elements and the charge contact elements from premature contact, misalignment, mechanical wear, or damage. Only when the contact device is correctly aligned and positioned does the guide device permit the intended electrical contact to be established.

Overall, the system provides a reliable and precise mechanism for connecting an electrically driven vehicle to a charging station. By combining vertical and horizontal positioning with guided contact formation, it supports safe, efficient, and rapid charging while reducing the risk of damage to the electrical contact components.
outputs.L4:
A quick-charging system for electric vehicles includes a stationary charging station and a contact device arranged on the vehicle. To establish a charging connection, the vehicle-side contact device is brought into alignment with a corresponding charging contact device of the stationary charging station. A positioning device is provided for this purpose and is configured to position the vehicle-side contact device both vertically and horizontally relative to the charging contact device. In this way, the electrical contacts of the two contact devices can be accurately aligned before the charging current is transferred.

The system further includes a guide device that controls the approach movement between the vehicle-side contact device and the charging contact device. The guide device ensures that the mechanical and electrical contact elements do not touch one another too early or in an incorrect position. Instead, the guide device guides the contact devices toward one another until a defined contact position is reached. Only when the charging contacts are correctly aligned and positioned are the electrical contact elements allowed to engage with each other.

This arrangement improves the reliability and safety of the charging process. By preventing premature contact, the system reduces the risk of arcing, mechanical damage, misalignment, or incomplete electrical connection. The positioning device compensates for deviations in the stopping position of the vehicle, while the guide device provides controlled movement into the final charging position. As a result, a stable and secure charging connection can be formed quickly and repeatedly, making the system particularly suitable for high-power charging of electric vehicles such as buses, commercial vehicles, and passenger cars.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be a small word, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It helps us point to something specific, something already known, or something unique. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that the listener understands.

This simple word gives clarity and direction. It appears in everyday speech, in titles, in stories, and in conversations. Without “the,” many sentences would sound incomplete or confusing. It helps connect ideas and makes communication more precise.

Although “the” is short and often unnoticed, it plays a powerful role. It reminds us that even the smallest words can carry great meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention involving a quick charging system for electric vehicles, where a movable contact device aligns vertically and horizontally with a stationary charging station contact device and uses guides to prevent premature contact.
counterfactuals.output: A quick charging system for an electric vehicle includes a stationary charging station contact device and a movable vehicle-side contact device configured to establish an electrical charging connection. The movable contact device is adjustable in both a vertical direction and a horizontal direction to align with corresponding contacts of the stationary contact device. One or more guide structures are provided to mechanically guide the movable contact device during approach and alignment, thereby correcting positional deviations between the vehicle and the charging station. The guide structures are configured to prevent electrical contact between the respective contact elements until a predetermined aligned position is reached, reducing the risk of arcing, wear, or improper engagement. Upon completion of alignment, the movable contact device is brought into conductive engagement with the stationary contact device to enable high-power charging of the electric vehicle.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal technical description of a rapid charging system for electrically driven vehicles, including a contact element carrier, charge contact elements, vertical/horizontal positioning, and a guide device that blocks contact until the contact position is reached.
counterfactuals.output:
A rapid charging system for electrically driven vehicles comprises a stationary charging interface configured to establish a high-current electrical connection with a corresponding vehicle-side charging interface. The charging interface includes a contact element carrier on which a plurality of charge contact elements are arranged. The charge contact elements are configured to transmit electrical charging current, in particular direct current for rapid charging of a traction battery of the vehicle.

The contact element carrier is mounted so as to be positionable relative to the vehicle-side charging interface. For this purpose, the rapid charging system includes a positioning mechanism configured to move the contact element carrier in at least one vertical direction and in at least one horizontal direction. The vertical positioning enables compensation of different vehicle heights or load-dependent height variations, while the horizontal positioning enables alignment of the charge contact elements with corresponding mating contact elements of the vehicle. The positioning mechanism may comprise one or more actuators, guide rails, lifting elements, sliding elements, or articulated supports, by means of which the contact element carrier can be displaced into a defined contact position.

The charge contact elements are preferably arranged on the contact element carrier in a predetermined contact pattern. Each charge contact element may be formed as a contact pin, contact plate, contact shoe, spring contact, or another electrically conductive contact body suitable for transmitting high charging currents. The charge contact elements may be resiliently mounted or provided with contact-pressure means in order to ensure reliable electrical contact when the contact position is reached.

The rapid charging system further comprises a guide device associated with the contact element carrier and/or with the charge contact elements. The guide device is configured to guide the relative movement between the stationary charging interface and the vehicle-side charging interface during approach. In particular, the guide device mechanically defines an insertion path or alignment path by which the contact element carrier is brought into the correct contact position relative to the mating contact elements.

The guide device is designed such that electrical contact between the charge contact elements and the corresponding mating contact elements is blocked until the contact element carrier has reached the defined contact position. For this purpose, the guide device may include blocking surfaces, guide contours, stops, shields, insulating barriers, or mechanically coupled locking elements that prevent premature engagement of the charge contact elements. Only after the contact element carrier has been moved into the correct vertical and horizontal alignment does the guide device permit the charge contact elements to enter into conductive engagement with the mating contact elements.

In one embodiment, the guide device comprises at least one guide member projecting beyond the charge contact elements in the direction of approach. The guide member first engages a corresponding receiving or guide structure on the vehicle. During further movement, the guide member centers and aligns the contact element carrier. Until this centering process is completed, the guide member or an associated blocking element maintains a physical separation between the charge contact elements and the mating contact elements. When the predetermined contact position is reached, the blocking element is released or displaced, thereby allowing the charge contact elements to engage the mating contact elements.

The rapid charging system may additionally include sensors for detecting the position of the contact element carrier, the alignment state, the presence of the vehicle, and/or the reaching of the contact position. A control unit may be provided to control the vertical and horizontal positioning mechanism on the basis of sensor signals. The control unit may also enable the charging current only after confirmation that the contact element carrier is in the contact position and that the guide device has permitted proper mechanical engagement of the charge contact elements.

By preventing electrical contact until the defined contact position is reached, the guide device reduces the risk of arcing, contact wear, misalignment, and damage to the charge contact elements. The system thereby enables reliable, repeatable, and safe rapid charging of electrically driven vehicles, particularly in applications requiring automated connection, such as buses, commercial vehicles, industrial vehicles, or autonomous electric vehicles.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an abstract for a patent application about forming an electrically conductive connection between an electric vehicle and a stationary charging station using movable contact devices, contact pairs, and a protective guide mechanism.
counterfactuals.output: An electric vehicle charging interface is disclosed for forming an electrically conductive connection between an electric vehicle and a stationary charging station. The interface includes at least one movable contact device arranged on one of the vehicle or the charging station and configured to move between a retracted position and a contacting position. The movable contact device carries one or more electrical contacts configured to engage complementary contacts of at least one contact pair on the other of the vehicle or charging station to transmit charging current and/or control signals. A protective guide mechanism is provided to guide relative movement of the movable contact device during approach and engagement, align the contacts of the contact pair, and shield the contacts from mechanical impact, contamination, or unintended contact when the movable contact device is not in the contacting position. The guide mechanism may include cooperating guide surfaces, housings, covers, or centering elements that facilitate reliable electrical connection during automated or assisted charging of the electric vehicle.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert these claim features into a single paragraph patent abstract: quick charging system for electric vehicles; contact device and charging contact device; positioning device for vertical and horizontal movement; contact elements on a carrier; contact pairs in the contact position; guide device preventing premature physical contact.
counterfactuals.output: A quick charging system for electric vehicles includes a contact device and a corresponding charging contact device configured to establish an electrical charging connection in a contact position. The system includes a positioning device arranged to move at least one of the contact device and the charging contact device vertically and horizontally relative to the other for alignment and connection. A plurality of contact elements are disposed on a carrier and are arranged to form respective contact pairs when the contact device and the charging contact device reach the contact position. A guide device is provided to guide relative movement of the contact device and the charging contact device and to prevent premature physical contact between the contact elements before proper alignment is achieved, thereby enabling reliable, controlled, and safe high-power charging of the electric vehicle.
